name: 4 Winds Championship
epitaph: The belt 4 Winds Wrestling crowned last and placed above the four compass titles it had run on since opening. Its own inaugural tournament ran across Maelstrom III: Legacy in March 2004 and finished with Jerms holding a trophy belt he used, minutes later, to club the night's guest referee in the back of the head.
notes: Receipted to the fed's own Maelstrom III: Legacy card and to Jerms' own roster card, which bills him "1st Ever 4 Winds Wrestling Champion (Won the Tourney at M3: Legacy, Current Champ)".

name: North Wind Championship
epitaph: 4 Winds Wrestling's own top singles belt from its first night. A gauntlet on the opening StormFront of July 2003 crowned Jay Phoenix as its first champion; the belt then changed hands four times in eight months, through Syxx Figures, Jaime, Todd Dream and Patti Anderson, and every one of those changes turned on outside interference the fed staged deliberately — a coal miner's glove, a run-in, a stablemate with a title belt in his hands, and finally a guest referee counting three.
notes: The awards site's own Hall of Fame ballot names "Jay Phoenix (First Ever NWT Champion)" and "Todd Dream (Longest Ever NWT Reign)"; the reign sequence below is built from the fed's own show scripts and the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html).

name: South Wind Championship
epitaph: The belt 4 Winds Wrestling gave its second division, decided in a ladder match at the end of a two-bracket tournament in July 2003 and held first by Patti Anderson. Its own record is the fed's busiest: a champion in the fed's own count went through it roughly every few weeks, and one holder wrote on the fed's own board that at the rate it moved there would be fifty-four South Wind champions in a year.
notes: Patti Anderson's own roster card bills her "First Ever South Wind Champion"; the later sequence is receipted to the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html).

name: East Wind Tag Team Championship
epitaph: 4 Winds Wrestling's tag titles, crowned at Maelstrom II: Eruption in December 2003 at the end of a gauntlet and a tournament final. The division they were built for kept emptying: in February 2005 the fed put the belts to a members' poll asking whether to keep them as tag titles, suspend them, or turn them into a ladies', pure-wrestling or cruiserweight championship, and its own owner argued to keep them on the ground that killing the tag division would cost 4WW its place in Primetime Central's.
notes: The poll and the argument are in the fed's own East Wind Title Situation thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-east-wind-title-situation.html).

name: West Wind Championship
epitaph: The fourth compass belt, and the one 4 Winds Wrestling booked for gimmick matches — its recorded changes include a Flaming Cross match and a two-out-of-three-falls bout fought over 220 light tubes and barbed-wire ropes with an I Quit third fall.
notes: The gimmick stipulations are quoted from the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html); the fed's own East Wind poll thread describes the belt's own booking as "the WWT's gimmick stuff".

name: Tempest Championship
epitaph: The belt named for the midweek show 4 Winds Wrestling ran for one month and then dropped. Tempest the programme was cancelled in August 2003 because a midweek deadline did not fit the roster's own schedules; the name came back as a championship, and the fed's own title historian could not find dates for its first two holders.
notes: The cancellation is announced in the fed's own Federation News of 2 August 2003; the missing early dates are stated as missing in the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html).
